title: Reconcile quota and rate-limit accounting for KV prefetch + coalesced batch aggregation
creator: Evan Park
description: There are recurring discrepancies between what customers are charged and the effective compute/throughput observed when requests hit prefix/KV caches and when our runtime coalesces many inflight requests into aggregated batches. This ticket defines a deterministic, auditable accounting model and implements telemetry and enforcement changes so quotas and rate limits reflect true customer usage without double-charging or undercounting cache-avoided work.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic per-request effective_token_count is computed and emitted regardless of whether the request was served from prefix cache, KV cache hit, or generated in an aggregated batch
Rate limiter enforcement (tokens/sec and concurrent request quotas) uses the emitted effective_token_count for quota consumption decisions and exposes events for denied requests with reason codes

Billing pipeline (metering aggregator) consumes the effective_token_count and three new flags (cache_hit=true|false, coalesced_batch_id or "none") to produce identical invoiceable totals as observed node-level compute metrics within a 2% margin in synthetic replay tests

Backwards-compatible behavior: for historical records where we lack flags, fallback to conservative billing (do not double-count prefetch overlaps), and provide a reconciliation job to fix prior invoices flagged by monitoring
Integration tests and end-to-end dashboards (console) added to show token distribution across cache hits, prefetches, and aggregated batches for a sample set of customers.
notes: Root causes identified in spike: (1) prefetch/KV cache short-circuit returns previously emitted a token count of 0 but upstream batching aggregated charge onto the initiator; (2) coalesced batch metering currently attributes total generated tokens to the batch leader request which can double-charge when leader also benefited from KV cache prefetch; (3) rate limiter sees only request count, not effective token weight, so high-token requests can bypass soft quotas under heavy coalescing.

Proposed model: every incoming logical request computes an effective_token_count defined as max(prefetch_saved_tokens ? 0 : predicted_generation_tokens, actual_generation_tokens_observed) with tags: cache_role={served_from_cache|prefetched|miss}, kv_cache_hit=true|false, batch_role={leader|participant|solo}, coalesced_batch_id=<uuid|none>. The runtime must emit these fields atomically to the metering hot path.

Charging rules: (A) If served entirely from prefix cache with zero generation, effective_token_count=0 and do not charge generation tokens. (B) If prefetch populated KV cache and later multiple participants hit that cached KV entry, charge the prefetch initiator for the upstream compute tokens and mark participants with cache_hit=true and zero generation charge. (C) For coalesced aggregated batches, split generated tokens proportionally to predicted/observed request weights; leader assignment is only for coordination, not charging, except when leader requested generation for itself.
implementation_steps: runtime: add per-request emission of effective_token_count, cache_role, kv_cache_hit, batch_role, coalesced_batch_id (atomic event) — PR runtime#2143
rate-limiter: switch to token-weighted quota deduction path; add per-request fast-path for small-cache-hit requests to skip heavy quota checks but still emit events — PR rl#328
metering pipeline: accept the new fields, apply aggregation rules (prefetch attribution, proportional split), and store invoiceable_token_count per request — PR billing#452
dashboards/tests: synthetic replay harness to validate invoiceable totals versus node-level compute; add console cards for top-n discrepancies — DOCS/dashboard#19
reconciliation job: batch job to scan last 90 days, detect likely double-charges caused by missing fields, and flag accounts for manual review/auto-credit where confidence>95% — JOB reconcile#03
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Emitting additional fields in hot path increases telemetry traffic and could add latency. Mitigation: pack fields into existing metering binary envelope and benchmark at 50k rps before rollout; feature flag rollout region-by-region

Risk: Incorrect proportional split algorithm could under/over-charge customers. Mitigation: start with conservative split (credit participants on any cache_hit) and iterate; run replay on shadow billing stream for two weeks before switching live invoicing

Risk: Edge cases where prefetch occurs in one region and participants hit in another causing attribution mismatch. Mitigation: include global coalesced_batch_id and leader origin, and use eventual reconciliation across regions with topology awareness
